name: Lard
label: Alternative Tentacles
lede: Jello Biafra showed up in Chicago with newspaper clippings instead of lyrics, and Ministry's engine room turned them into a band that never really toured.

eras.title: Clippings instead of lyrics
eras.text: Jello Biafra had been out of Dead Kennedys for two years when he ended up in Chicago with the Ministry crew. The first Lard sessions started with a name, a stack of newspaper cuttings and a studio owner who would soon end up on a record sleeve.

years.big: Al fell on the floor laughing
years.src: Punknews: Jello Biafra Walks Us Through · Wikipedia: Lard (band)
yt: Lard: Ministry and Dead Kennedys unite
years.h: The name arrives in one second flat
years.p: [[Jello Biafra|2280ca0e-6968-4349-8c36-cb0cbd6ee95f]] says "Lard" was the first thing that popped into his head when [[Al Jourgensen|6c0dadab-266a-4601-8394-5b8e19e90def]] asked what to call it, and Jourgensen's reaction settled the matter.
years.xp:
Biafra told Punknews that the name came straight out of his head, and that Jourgensen laughed so hard he ended up on the floor. Wikipedia dates the band's founding to 1988, when it started as a side project with Jourgensen, bassist [[Paul Barker|5bec856f-b78b-4216-8af5-1c0c6365bcbe]] and drummer [[Jeff Ward|90023d8a-3907-45ec-a2aa-b8da61a6d0bd]], all from the [[Ministry|13df2a46-f72f-40e7-aa63-26fcf62c7048]] orbit.

Biafra also said he had heard Ministry's records and knew he had to work with Jourgensen again, a hint that the two had crossed paths before Lard.

years.cap: Chicago Trax, where Lard cut its first EP
years.src: Punknews: Jello Biafra Walks Us Through · Wikipedia: The Power of Lard
years.h: Biafra brings Chicago Tribune cuttings to Chicago Trax
years.p: He turned up with no lyrics, only remembered one-liners and clippings from the Chicago Tribune, and recorded the first Lard EP at the studio Ministry used.
years.xp:
In Biafra's own account to Punknews, the raw material for the first EP was "one liners that I remembered or things that I cut out of the Chicago Tribune." Only afterwards did he notice the songs shared a theme: controlling people through anxiety about how they look.

Wikipedia lists the recording at Chicago Trax Studios in 1988, with the producer credits going to Hypo Luxa, Hermes Pan and Count Ringworm. Reid Hyams, who co-owned the studio and produced the first EP, would get his name into a Lard album title two years later.

years.h: The Power of Lard: a three-track EP with a 31-minute closer
years.p: The debut on Alternative Tentacles runs 43 minutes on three tracks, and "Time to Melt" alone takes 31:55.
years.xp:
The EP has the title track (7:29), "Hellfudge" (5:04) and "Time to Melt". Wikipedia says it reached number 4 on the UK Indie Chart. Trouser Press called it "a casual and exciting bit of supergrouping"; Music Week's Jerry Smith found it "rather predictable."

The title track found a second audience in 1996, when it soundtracked a section of the skateboard video Toy Machine: Welcome to Hell, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Reid's picture on the back
eras.text: Lard got its first live outings as guests on Ministry's own shows, then made a full album in the same Chicago studio. The drummer's chair started to be shared.

years.src: Wikipedia: In Case You Didn't Feel Like Showing Up · Wikipedia: Lard (band)
yt: Ministry with Jello Biafra: The Power of Lard, Feb 22 1990
years.h: Biafra walks on at Merrillville and reads his own Pledge of Allegiance
years.p: Partway through Ministry's set, after "Stigmata", Jello Biafra came out and delivered his rewrite of the Pledge, then stayed for a Lard song.
years.xp:
The show at Holiday Star Theatre in Merrillville, Indiana, became Ministry's live album In Case You Didn't Feel Like Showing Up, released September 4, 1990. Wikipedia notes the video mixes that night with a December 1989 New Year's Eve show in Chicago, and the band had to wear identical clothes on both dates so the edit would match.

Lard played during Ministry's 1988 tour and throughout its 1989 and 1990 dates, according to Wikipedia. "The Power of Lard" is credited to Jourgensen, Barker, Ward and Biafra on the 2017 reissue, running 8:11 live.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Last Temptation of Reid · Punknews: Jello Biafra Walks Us Through
years.h: The Last Temptation of Reid puts the studio manager on the sleeve
years.p: The first Lard album is named after Reid Hyams, the Chicago Trax co-owner and producer of the EP, and his photo is on the back cover.
years.xp:
Recorded in May 1990 at Chicago Trax and released on Alternative Tentacles, it takes its title from the Scorsese film with Reid swapped in. It includes a reworked "They're Coming to Take Me Away, Ha-Haaa!" with guitar added and an extra verse by Biafra. Vinyl runs 41:38, the CD and cassette 56:07, and Wikipedia says the album reached number 69 on the UK Albums Chart.

Biafra told Punknews the sessions could resemble "a Marx brothers movie," and that Reid was forced to pose for the back cover. "Forkboy" later reached a wider audience through the Natural Born Killers soundtrack.

eras.title: The drummer
eras.text: Ministry became huge and Lard went quiet, and then the band lost the drummer who had been there from the first sessions.

years.src: Wikipedia: Jeff Ward (musician) · Ministry Music: Jeff Ward Obituary
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Ward died by suicide by carbon monoxide poisoning in Chicago; he had played on the first Lard EP and album.
years.xp:
Ward had played with Ministry, Revolting Cocks and [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]], and sang and drummed in Lard. A Ministry fan-site obituary citing the Chicago Sun-Times (May 6, 1993) says he died at his West Side home, that he had struggled with addiction, and quotes his brother Jason. A tribute concert was held at the Thirsty Whale in River Grove, Illinois, where Ward had played as a teenager.

Revolting Cocks' Linger Ficken' Good (1993) and Ministry's Filth Pig (1996) carry dedications to him, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Last Temptation of Reid
years.h: "Forkboy" lands on the Natural Born Killers soundtrack
years.p: The opening track of The Last Temptation of Reid reached far more people through the film, and has since been covered by Flotsam and Jetsam and Black Light Burns.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits the film soundtrack for the wider recognition of "Forkboy," which has since been covered by Flotsam and Jetsam and Black Light Burns.

eras.title: Seven years to finish a record
eras.text: Pure Chewing Satisfaction and 70's Rock Must Die came out of sessions spread across a decade, with Bill Rieflin behind the kit and Ward's earlier tracks folded in.

years.src: Wikipedia: Pure Chewing Satisfaction · Brainwashed: Pure Chewing Satisfaction review
yt: Lard: Pure Chewing Satisfaction, full album
years.p: The second Lard album was built from recordings made in May 1990, 1991 to 1992 and 1995 to 1997 at Chicago Trax, with a 30-page insert of absurd newspaper clippings.
years.xp:
Bill Rieflin drums on most tracks, with Ward and Rey Washam on some and Mike Scaccia guitar on several songs. The Fort Worth Star-Telegram called the sound "Ministry's 'Just One Fix' times eight"; NME gave it 8 out of 10.

Brainwashed's reviewer liked the packaging, a 30-page insert that recalls the collage style of [[Dead Kennedys|37c78aeb-d196-42b5-b991-6afb4fc9bc2e]] releases, and found some tracks repetitive.

years.src: Alternative Tentacles: Lard · Wikipedia: 70's Rock Must Die
years.h: 70's Rock Must Die, and a 1979 Ford Pinto for sale
years.p: The three-track EP ends with "Ballad of Marshall Ledbetter", inspired by a real protest in the Florida state capitol.
years.xp:
Alternative Tentacles says the release came with an auction of a vintage 1979 Ford Pinto with period-appropriate decor. The tracks are "70s Rock Must Die" (7:07), "Volcanus 2000 (We Wipe the World)" (6:14) and the Ledbetter song (5:06).

Wikipedia says it draws on the same sessions as the last album, and lists Metal Hammer's 8 out of 10.

eras.title: Not quite dead
eras.text: The band never officially toured. It came back for a handful of shows, lost another drummer and keeps getting announced as coming back.

years.h: Lard closes a Ministry show in Los Angeles
years.p: Biafra, Jourgensen and Barker played a Lard set at the end of Ministry's March 2003 Los Angeles concert.

years.h: Lard plays San Francisco, Portland and Seattle
years.p: Three Ministry dates in September 2004 (San Francisco on the 26th, Portland the 28th, Seattle the 29th) included Lard appearances.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists these as the only other Lard shows besides the 1988 to 1990 Ministry tours and the 2003 Los Angeles date. As of 2007, Antiwarsongs described the band as having never launched an official tour.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Bill Rieflin · BNR Metal Pages: Lard
years.h: Bill Rieflin, drummer on the last two Lard records, dies at 59
years.p: Ministry called him "an integral part of Ministry's developments and success" after his death in March 2020.
years.xp: Rieflin played on Pure Chewing Satisfaction and 70's Rock Must Die, and later played with R.E.M. and King Crimson. Rolling Stone's report gives no cause of death.

q: His brain is different than most brains, man.
years.src: Wikipedia: Lard (band) · Stereogum: We've Got A File On You · Jello Biafra's Renegade Roundtable
years.h: Jourgensen says a new Lard album is coming
years.p: He said he and Biafra would email songs back and forth to make it, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Jourgensen told Stereogum in 2024 that he and Biafra still hook up in a studio whenever they are in the same town, and said of Biafra: "His brain is different than most brains, man." The first episode of Biafra's Renegade Roundtable podcast, released October 21, 2022, was a conversation with Jourgensen that touches on Lard.

years.h: Paul Barker rejoins Al Jourgensen for a final Ministry album
years.p: The bassist who had been in Lard since the start returned to the Ministry fold in March 2024, per Wikipedia, after years of saying they would not work together.
years.xp: Barker said in 2015 that he was "fairly confident we will not work together," but the two reconciled at documentary screenings in 2018, according to Wikipedia. Jourgensen has also suggested one final Lard album is possible, per AllMusic and Antiwarsongs.
